81158.subject: Technical Drawing
81158.question_text: Construct a regular hexagon with a side length of 30 mm using the circumscribed circle method. Show all construction lines clearly.
81158.explanation:
1. Draw a circle with a radius of 30 mm (since the side of a regular hexagon equals the radius of its circumscribed circle).
2. Mark a point on the circumference as one vertex of the hexagon.
3. Using a compass set to 30 mm, step off five more points around the circumference.
4. Connect the six points with straight lines to form the hexagon.
5. Ensure all construction lines (e.g., the circle and compass arcs) are visible and labeled where necessary.

81159.subject: Technical Drawing
81159.question_text:
Given the front and side views of a block in first-angle orthographic projection (as shown below), draw the plan view.
Note: Assume the front view shows a rectangle 50 mm wide and 30 mm high, and the side view shows a rectangle 40 mm deep and 30 mm high.
81159.explanation:
1. Analyze the front and side views to determine the dimensions of the block: 50 mm (width) × 40 mm (depth) × 30 mm (height).
2. Draw the plan view as a rectangle with dimensions 50 mm (width) × 40 mm (depth).
3. Ensure the plan view aligns correctly with the front and side views in first-angle projection (plan below front view, side view to the right of the front view).
4. Label all views and dimensions clearly.

81160.subject: Technical Drawing
81160.question_text: Construct an external tangent to two circles with diameters 40 mm and 20 mm, respectively, and centers 60 mm apart. Show all construction lines.
81160.explanation:
1. Draw the two circles with diameters 40 mm and 20 mm, and centers 60 mm apart.
2. Draw a line connecting the centers of the two circles.
3. Construct a circle with radius equal to the difference of the two radii (20 mm - 10 mm = 10 mm) centered at the larger circle's center.
4. Construct a tangent from the smaller circle's center to this new circle.
5. Extend the radius of the larger circle to meet the tangent point.
6. Draw a line parallel to this radius through the tangent point to form the external tangent.
7. Ensure all construction lines are visible and labeled.

81161.subject: Technical Drawing
81161.question_text:
Draw a full sectional front view of the object shown in the pictorial view below, assuming the cutting plane passes through the center of the object.
Note: The object is a hollow cylinder with an external diameter of 50 mm, internal diameter of 30 mm, and height of 40 mm, with a 10 mm thick base.
81161.explanation:
1. Draw the full sectional front view by removing the front half of the object.
2. Show the external and internal diameters (50 mm and 30 mm) as concentric circles in the section.
3. Represent the base as a rectangle 10 mm thick at the bottom.
4. Use hatching to indicate the cut surfaces (45° lines spaced 2-3 mm apart).
5. Label all dimensions and ensure the section aligns with standard conventions.

81162.subject: Technical Drawing
81162.question_text: Draw an isometric view of a rectangular block with dimensions 60 mm (length) × 40 mm (width) × 30 mm (height). Include all construction lines.
81162.explanation:
1. Draw the isometric axes at 30° to the horizontal.
2. Mark the length (60 mm) along the 30° axis to the right.
3. Mark the width (40 mm) along the 30° axis to the left.
4. Mark the height (30 mm) vertically from the origin.
5. Complete the block by drawing parallel lines to form the top and side faces.
6. Ensure all construction lines (e.g., axes and guide lines) are visible and labeled.

81163.subject: Technical Drawing
81163.question_text: Develop the lateral surface of a right circular cone with a base diameter of 50 mm and a slant height of 60 mm. Show all construction lines.
81163.explanation:
1. Calculate the circumference of the base: $C = \pi imes d = \pi imes 50$ mm.
2. Draw a sector of a circle with radius equal to the slant height (60 mm) and arc length equal to the circumference of the base.
3. The angle of the sector can be calculated using: $ heta = rac{C}{2 \pi r} imes 360° = rac{50 imes 360°}{2 imes 60} = 150°$.
4. Draw the sector with the calculated angle and radius.
5. Ensure all construction lines (e.g., sector radius and arc) are visible and labeled.

81164.subject: Technical Drawing
81164.question_text:
Given the front and plan views of an object in first-angle orthographic projection (as shown below), draw the side view.
Note: The front view shows a rectangle 40 mm wide and 20 mm high with a semicircle on top, and the plan view shows a rectangle 40 mm wide and 30 mm deep.
81164.explanation:
1. Analyze the front and plan views to determine the object's shape: a rectangular block with a semicircular top.
2. Draw the side view as a rectangle 30 mm deep and 20 mm high, with a semicircle on top.
3. Ensure the side view aligns correctly with the front and plan views in first-angle projection.
4. Label all views and dimensions clearly.

81165.subject: Technical Drawing
81165.question_text: Which of the following is the correct method for dimensioning a circle in a technical drawing?
81165.explanation: The correct method for dimensioning a circle is to use the diameter symbol (⌀) followed by the dimension value. This is the standard convention for circular features in technical drawings.

options.text: Using the radius symbol (R) followed by the dimension
Using the diameter symbol (⌀) followed by the dimension
Writing the dimension without any symbol
Using the circumference symbol (C) followed by the dimension

81166.subject: Technical Drawing
81166.question_text: Draw the line of interpenetration between a vertical cylinder (diameter 40 mm) and a horizontal cylinder (diameter 30 mm) whose axes intersect at right angles. Show all construction lines.
81166.explanation:
1. Draw the orthographic views (front and plan) of the two intersecting cylinders.
2. In the plan view, divide the circumference of the vertical cylinder into 12 equal parts.
3. Project these points to the front view and mark their intersections with the horizontal cylinder.
4. Draw a smooth curve through these points to represent the line of interpenetration.
5. Ensure all construction lines (e.g., division points and projections) are visible and labeled.

81167.subject: Technical Drawing
81167.question_text: Determine the true shape of the section obtained by cutting a right circular cone (base diameter 50 mm, height 60 mm) with an inclined plane passing through the midpoint of the axis and inclined at 45° to the base. Show all construction lines.
81167.explanation:
1. Draw the front and plan views of the cone.
2. Draw the inclined cutting plane in the front view.
3. Divide the base of the cone into 12 equal parts and project these to the front view.
4. Find the points of intersection between the cutting plane and the generators of the cone.
5. Project these points to the plan view to determine the true shape of the section (an ellipse).
6. Draw the ellipse in the plan view and ensure all construction lines are visible and labeled.
